a_rows_sample.anchor: Non-Negativity: cr(P)>=0. Normality: cr(T)=1 for tautology T. Finite Additivity: cr(P v Q)=cr(P)+cr(Q) for mutually exclusive P,Q. Consequences: Negation cr(~P)=1-cr(P). Maximality cr(P)<=1. Contradiction cr(F)=0. Entailment: P|=Q implies cr(P)<=cr(Q). Equivalence: P==Q implies cr(P)=cr(Q). General Additivity: cr(P v Q)=cr(P)+cr(Q)-cr(P^Q). Decomposition: cr(P)=cr(P^Q)+cr(P^~Q). Partition: sum_i cr(P_i)=1.
a_rows_sample.statement: Extracts the Kolmogorov probability axioms (Non-Negativity, Normality, Finite Additivity) and eight derived consequences (Negation, Maximality, Contradiction, Entailment, Equivalence, General Additivity, Decomposition, Partition) verbatim from the external source, each stated as a formal credence (cr) rule.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Ratio Formula: cr(P|Q)=cr(P^Q)/cr(Q) if cr(Q)>0. Conditional credences supervene on unconditional credences. Bayes's Theorem: cr(H|E)=cr(E|H)*cr(H)/cr(E), with expanded catchall form and multiple-hypotheses form cr(H_i|E)=cr(E|H_i)cr(H_i)/sum_j cr(E|H_j)cr(H_j). Conditionalization: cr_j(H)=cr_i(H|E) for evidence E learned between t_i and t_j with cr_i(E)>0, equivalently cr_j(H)=cr_i(H^E)/cr_i(E).
a_rows_sample.statement: Extracts the Ratio Formula (cr(P|Q)=cr(P^Q)/cr(Q)), Bayes's Theorem in three forms (basic, expanded-with-catchall, multiple-hypotheses), and Conditionalization (the diachronic updating rule cr_j(H)=cr_i(H|E)) verbatim from the source.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Law of Total Probability: cr(P)=sum_i cr(P|Q_i)*cr(Q_i) for a finite partition {Q_1,...,Q_n}, with conditional form. Probabilistic Independence: cr(P|Q)=cr(P), equivalent forms cr(P|Q)=cr(P|~Q) and cr(Q|P)=cr(Q); Multiplication Rule cr(P^Q)=cr(P)*cr(Q); General conjunction rule cr(P^Q)=cr(P|Q)*cr(Q). Conditional Independence: cr(P|Q^R)=cr(P|R). Screening Off: R screens off P from Q when cr(P|Q)!=cr(P) but cr(P|Q^R)=cr(P|R) and cr(P|Q^~R)=cr(P|~R).
a_rows_sample.statement: Extracts the Law of Total Probability, Probabilistic Independence (with three equivalent forms and the Multiplication Rule), Conditional Independence, and Screening Off, all verbatim from the source.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Regularity Principle: in a rational credence distribution, no logically contingent proposition receives unconditional credence 0: cr(P)>0 for all contingent P. Principal Principle: cr(A|Ch_i(A)=x ^ E)=x for admissible information E, with weighted average form cr(A|E)=sum_i x_i*cr(Ch(A)=x_i|E). Reflection Principle: cr_i(A|cr_j(A)=x)=x for t_i<t_j.
a_rows_sample.statement: Extracts the Regularity Principle (no contingent proposition gets credence 0), the Principal Principle (credence conditional on known objective chance equals that chance, with a weighted-average form), and the Reflection Principle (an agent should defer to its own known future credence) verbatim from the source.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Jeffrey Conditionalization: cr_j(A)=sum_i cr_i(A|B_i)*cr_j(B_i) for a finite partition {B_1,...,B_n}, with Rigidity Condition cr_j(A|B_i)=cr_i(A|B_i). Countable Additivity: cr(Q_1 v Q_2 v ...)=sum_{i=1}^infinity cr(Q_i) for a countable set of mutually exclusive propositions. Conglomerability: inf_i cr(P|Q_i) <= cr(P) <= sup_i cr(P|Q_i) for each proposition P and partition {Q_1,Q_2,...}; Finite Conglomerability follows from the axioms via the Law of Total Probability.
a_rows_sample.statement: Extracts Jeffrey Conditionalization (updating without certainty, via a rigidity condition), Countable Additivity (extending finite additivity to countably infinite partitions), and Conglomerability (credence bounded between the infimum and supremum of its partition-conditional values) verbatim from the source.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Derivation of Bayes's Theorem: Step 1, by the Ratio Formula cr(H|E)=cr(H^E)/cr(E). Step 2, by the Ratio Formula symmetric, cr(E^H)=cr(E|H)*cr(H). Step 3, since H^E == E^H, cr(H|E)=cr(E|H)*cr(H)/cr(E). ... Certainties are Created: if E is learned between t_i,t_j then cr_j(E)=cr_i(E|E)=1. Certainties are Retained: if cr_i(H)=1 then cr_j(H)=1. Conditionalization is Cumulative: conditionalizing on E then E' equals conditionalizing on E^E'. Conditionalization is Commutative: update on E then E' equals update on E' then E.
a_rows_sample.statement: Reproduces the three-step derivation of Bayes's Theorem from the Ratio Formula, and four derived properties of Conditionalization: certainties are created (learned evidence becomes certain), certainties are retained (once credence 1, always credence 1 under conditionalization), conditionalization is cumulative (sequential conditionalization on E then E' equals conditionalizing on their conjunction), and conditionalization is commutative (update order does not matter) -- all reproduced verbatim from the source.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Odds(P)=cr(P):cr(~P). Odds_against(P)=cr(~P):cr(P). Bayes Factor: Odds_j(H)=Odds_i(H)*[cr_i(E|H)/cr_i(E|~H)], where Bayes Factor = cr_i(E|H)/cr_i(E|~H).
a_rows_sample.statement: Extracts the odds formulation of credence (Odds(P), Odds against P) and the Bayes Factor update rule (Odds_j(H)=Odds_i(H) times the Bayes Factor cr_i(E|H)/cr_i(E|~H)) verbatim from the source.

a_rows_sample.anchor: KnowledgeOS Application, Part 6: Bayesian epistemology principles -- agents have doxastic attitudes representable by real numbers; rational requirements are mathematical constraints closely related to the probability calculus. Sigma_t = Epistemic State = Credence Distribution. Probability table: a probability table assigns unconditional credences to each member of a partition (2x2 example, a+b+c+d=1). KnowledgeOS Application: K_t can be represented as a probability distribution over a propositional language L; Sigma_t is the credence distribution at time t. Five Core Bayesian Rules mapped: Non-Negativity, Normality, Finite Additivity, Ratio Formula (all Synchronic), Conditionalization (Diachronic) -- each mapped directly to a Sigma_t component.
a_rows_sample.statement: Asserts, without hedging, that Sigma_t (Epistemic State) = Credence Distribution, and that K_t (Knowledge State) can be represented directly as a probability distribution over a propositional language L, mapping five core Bayesian rules (Non-Negativity, Normality, Finite Additivity, Ratio Formula, Conditionalization) one-to-one onto Sigma_t components -- presented as an established application rather than a tested hypothesis, unlike the parallel Gita-kernel thread's disciplined candidate/hypothesis framing of its own Sigma-based formalizations.

a_rows_sample.anchor: The Hypothetical Priors Theorem: given any finite series of credence distributions each satisfying the axioms and Ratio Formula, if each cr_i is related to cr_{i+1} by Conditionalization, then there exists at least one regular probability distribution Pr_H such that cr_i(.)=Pr_H(.|E_i) for all i, where E_i is total evidence at t_i. KnowledgeOS Application: the epistemic standards of the system can be represented by a hypothetical prior Pr_H. The Knowledge State K_t is Pr_H conditionalized on total evidence E_t.
a_rows_sample.statement: Extracts the Hypothetical Priors Theorem (any consistent finite sequence of conditionalized credence distributions can be represented as one regular hypothetical prior conditionalized on accumulated evidence) and applies it to propose that KnowledgeOS's epistemic standards be represented as a single hypothetical prior Pr_H, with K_t = Pr_H conditionalized on total evidence E_t.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Relevance as Conditional Dependence: P relevant to Q iff cr(P|Q)!=cr(P). Screening Off in Causal Models: cr(P|Q^R)=cr(P|R); KnowledgeOS Application: the Lord Lens can use screening off to identify candidate causal explanations. Simpson's Paradox: cr(P|Q)>cr(P) but for all R_i, cr(P|Q^R_i)<cr(P|R_i); KnowledgeOS Application: the Zero Lens must detect Simpson's Paradox situations to avoid incorrect inferences from aggregated data.
a_rows_sample.statement: Defines relevance as conditional dependence (P relevant to Q iff cr(P|Q)!=cr(P)) and applies screening-off to a proposed 'Lord Lens' for candidate causal explanation. Flags Simpson's Paradox (a correlation reversing under every stratification) as a required detection target for the Zero Lens, to avoid incorrect inferences from aggregated data -- a genuine statistical hazard worth preserving even independent of the surrounding overclaiming pattern.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Part 14 Key Insights: Credences are the Epistemic State -- the book establishes credences are the fundamental epistemic state; KnowledgeOS can use credences as the representation of Sigma_t. Updating is Conditionalization -- rational updating is Conditionalization; KnowledgeOS can use this as the transition mechanism delta. Evidence is Certainty -- evidence becomes certain; used to model evidence ingestion. Priors Represent Epistemic Standards -- hypothetical priors represent epistemic standards; models the system's invariant epistemic posture. Relevance is Conditional Dependence -- used for the Zero Lens (gap detection) and Lord Lens (candidate generation).
a_rows_sample.statement: States five key insights, presented as established: credences are the epistemic state (representing Sigma_t); rational updating is Conditionalization (the transition mechanism delta); evidence becomes certain upon learning (models evidence ingestion); hypothetical priors represent the system's invariant epistemic standards/posture; relevance as conditional dependence underlies both a 'Zero Lens' (gap detection) and a 'Lord Lens' (candidate generation) -- again asserted directly rather than flagged as hypotheses pending independent derivation.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Final Statement: The Bayesian formalism provides a complete mathematical foundation for KnowledgeOS's epistemic state, updating mechanism, evidence handling, and inference engine. The core equations are: K_t = Probability Distribution over L. K_{t+1}=K_t(.|E_t). cr_t(H|E)=cr_t(E|H)*cr_t(H)/cr_t(E). cr_j(A)=sum_i cr_i(A|B_i)*cr_j(B_i). These are now formally available to KnowledgeOS. Status: COMPLETE -- FORMAL DERIVATIONS EXTRACTED.
a_rows_sample.statement: Closes with an unqualified claim that the Bayesian formalism provides 'a complete mathematical foundation' for KnowledgeOS's epistemic state, updating mechanism, evidence handling, and inference engine, restating four core equations (K_t as a probability distribution, K_{t+1} as conditionalization, Bayes's theorem, Jeffrey conditionalization) as 'now formally available to KnowledgeOS,' with final status 'COMPLETE -- FORMAL DERIVATIONS EXTRACTED' -- an unhedged completion claim of exactly the kind the parallel Gita-kernel research thread in this batch repeatedly identifies, audits, and corrects when made by other sources (e.g. S2281's HPA assessment, later rejected by S2282; the external_research lane's 'Solved/Complete' claims found 0-of-13 in the closure register throughout artifacts 18-37).

b_rows_sample.anchor: This volume provides the philosophical justification, applications, and alternatives for the Bayesian framework.
b_rows_sample.statement: Executive summary: Titelbaum's Volume 2 supplies Confirmation Theory, Decision Theory, Arguments for Bayesianism (Representation Theorems, Dutch Books, Accuracy Arguments), Challenges (Old Evidence, Logical Omniscience, Problem of the Priors), Alternatives (Comparative Confidence, Ranged Credences, Dempster-Shafer), Self-Locating Beliefs, and treatment of Equality/Identity, all claimed directly applicable to KnowledgeOS's epistemic architecture.

b_rows_sample.anchor: The Bayesian formalism provides a complete mathematical foundation for KnowledgeOS's epistemic state, updating mechanism, confirmation theory, decision theory, and justification.
b_rows_sample.statement: The document's culminating 'complete formal system for KnowledgeOS': Sigma_t = {cr_t(P): P in L} as the epistemic state; Sigma_{t+1} = Sigma_t(.|E_t) (or Jeffrey Conditionalization for uncertain evidence) as the transition; confirmation as E confirms H iff Sigma_t(H|E) > Sigma_t(H); decision as a_t = argmax_A sum_i u(A&S_i)*Sigma_t(S_i|A) (EDT) or the CDT analogue; and the Three Lenses re-stated as Zero (regularity/confirmation-measures/Scott Axiom), Lord (Bayes's theorem/likelihood ratios), Sarathi (decision theory/Conditionalization). Final claim: 'These are now formally available to KnowledgeOS' -- asserted without independent derivation or proof of fit to the prior KnowledgeOS kernel formalizations.

Note: S2305's HPA analysis of Titelbaum (2022) Fundamentals of Bayesian Epistemology 2 (Arguments/Challenges/Alternatives), companion to the B0055 Volume-1 mapping (S2304); possibly the same overall source-extraction object continued as a second volume, possibly a distinct document -- flagged POSSIBLY since B0055 registered the Volume-1 document under a similar label and this batch does not resolve whether they should merge.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Human first has/conceives an Ideal State ... IDEAL STATE -> EXPECTATIONS/CRITERIA -> OBSERVATION -> COMPARISON -> DETERMINATION -> FACT/KNOWLEDGE. That is a substantially different model from the one I was using before.
a_rows_sample.statement: Major reorientation: humans do not build up an ideal state from arbitrary observations; instead a human first has/conceives an Ideal State and then evaluates reality against it, giving the pipeline IDEAL STATE -> EXPECTATIONS/CRITERIA -> OBSERVATION -> COMPARISON -> DETERMINATION -> FACT/KNOWLEDGE, substantially reversing the previously-used observation-first model.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Ideal state ... The complete state of what is supposed to be known/true/valid for the thing at that point in time. ... all applicable rules; all required participants; ... I_t = Ideal Knowledge State at t ... O_t -- comparison with I_t --> K_t
a_rows_sample.statement: Defines the ideal state I_t broadly as the complete state of what is supposed to be known/true/valid for a thing at time t; for an election system this would include all applicable rules, required participants, required conditions, valid relationships, required evidence, expected states, constraints, applicable laws, and known principles; every new piece of observed information O_t is evaluated against I_t, giving the extraction problem O_t --comparison with I_t--> K_t.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Information that correctly describes some aspect of the ideal state is Knowledge. ... K_t subset I_t ... The ideal state itself may be unknown to us. ... I_t -- the theoretical ideal state, and hat-I_t -- our current extracted/estimated representation of it. Then: hat-I_t != I_t in general. That may actually explain your earlier statement: "We try our best but never achieve the best."
a_rows_sample.statement: Refines 'information on the ideal state is knowledge' to 'information that correctly describes some aspect of the ideal state is Knowledge', giving K_t subset-or-equal I_t as the established/identified portion of the ideal state -- but the ideal state I_t itself may be unknown to us, so we must distinguish the theoretical ideal state I_t from our current extracted/estimated representation hat-I_t, with hat-I_t != I_t in general, explaining 'we try our best but never achieve the best'.

a_rows_sample.anchor: P(x|O_{<=t},I_t^known) ... Probability is involved in extracting the ideal state from imperfect observations. Not: Knowledge=Probability. Instead: Probability models the uncertainty of our extraction of the ideal state.
a_rows_sample.statement: Locates probability's role: for an ideal-state element x, given incomplete and overlapping observations O_1..O_n we estimate P(x|O_{<=t},I_t^known); probability is involved in extracting the ideal state from imperfect observations, not in defining Knowledge -- probability models the uncertainty of our extraction of the ideal state, not Knowledge itself.

a_rows_sample.anchor: System must have backup capability ... backup configuration exists ... If the applicable reasoning rules determine that the observation satisfies the criterion, we establish: F_t: "System has backup capability." ... the fact is not produced merely from the observation. It is produced by: Observation + Ideal State + Comparison Criteria + Reasoning.
a_rows_sample.statement: Worked example of fact production: ideal state I_t requires 'system must have backup capability', observation O_t is 'backup configuration exists'; comparing O_t against I_t via applicable reasoning rules establishes fact F_t='System has backup capability' -- a fact is produced not merely from observation but from Observation + Ideal State + Comparison Criteria + Reasoning together.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Logic = mechanism for comparing/deriving consequences from the ideal state and observed state. ... I_t: A and B and C. Observed: O_t: A,B,not-C. Logic gives: O_t does not entail I_t. Therefore the determination might be: F_t: "Current state does not satisfy the ideal state."
a_rows_sample.statement: Defines logic's role as the mechanism for comparing/deriving consequences from the ideal state and observed state: given ideal state I_t=(A and B and C) and observed O_t=(A,B,not-C), logic determines O_t does not entail I_t, yielding determination F_t='Current state does not satisfy the ideal state'.

a_rows_sample.anchor: P(A)=1, P(B)=0.9, P(C)=0.6, P(D)=0.2. Then our extracted representation of the ideal/current relationship is uncertain. The probability is therefore attached to the extraction/determination, not necessarily to the underlying ideal state itself. That gives: I_t -> hat-I_t where hat-I_t is probabilistically estimated from available information.
a_rows_sample.statement: Explains the origin of graded 0-to-1 values: if the ideal state requires A,B,C,D but observations only partially resolve them (P(A)=1,P(B)=0.9,P(C)=0.6,P(D)=0.2), the extracted representation of the ideal/current relationship is uncertain -- this probability attaches to the extraction/determination I_t -> hat-I_t, not to the underlying ideal state itself.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Where does the Ideal State come from? ... A. Given by reality I_t=Reality_t B. Given by human knowledge I_t=HumanModel_t C. Given by rules/laws/principles I_t=NormativeModel_t D. Given by the domain model I_t=DomainModel_t E. An ideal mathematical state I_t=I* F. Some combination I_t=f(Reality,Rules,Principles,Domain,HumanKnowledge). We should not assume which one it is.
a_rows_sample.statement: Poses 'Where does the Ideal State come from?' as, in the author's opinion, the most important unresolved problem, with six unassumed candidate sources: given by reality (I_t=Reality_t), given by human knowledge (I_t=HumanModel_t), given by rules/laws/principles (I_t=NormativeModel_t), given by the domain model (I_t=DomainModel_t), an ideal mathematical state (I_t=I*), or some combination I_t=f(Reality,Rules,Principles,Domain,HumanKnowledge) -- explicitly: we should not assume which one it is.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Knowledge = identified elements/relationships of an ideal state. And the current Knowledge state is K_t while the ideal state is I_t. The goal of knowledge extraction could therefore be: K_t -> I_t or more realistically: K_t approx I_t with the difference I_t - K_t representing what remains unknown, uncertain, or unextracted.
a_rows_sample.statement: Resolves 'is Knowledge a collection of facts?' into a richer formulation: Knowledge = identified elements/relationships of an ideal state; with current knowledge state K_t and ideal state I_t, knowledge extraction aims at K_t -> I_t or more realistically K_t approx I_t, with the residual I_t - K_t representing what remains unknown, uncertain, or unextracted.

a_rows_sample.anchor: "Every information on the ideal state of anything is knowledge." I would change "every information" to "every correctly determined proposition about the ideal state". ... "I believe the ideal state contains X." That is information about someone's belief, not necessarily Knowledge about the ideal state. ... "The document says X." ... Information about an ideal state != Knowledge of the ideal state.
a_rows_sample.statement: Challenges the overbroad claim 'every information on the ideal state of anything is knowledge', proposing instead 'every correctly determined proposition about the ideal state'; example: 'I believe the ideal state contains X' is information about someone's belief, not Knowledge about the ideal state, and 'the document says X' is knowledge that the document says X, not knowledge that X is true. Preserves the distinction: Information about an ideal state != Knowledge of the ideal state.

a_rows_sample.anchor: IDEAL STATE -> (defines expected/relevant structure) -> OBSERVED REALITY -> INFORMATION -> EXTRACTION -> (evidence/uncertainty) -> COMPARISON (ideal <-> observed) -> LOGIC -> DETERMINATION -> FACTS -> KNOWLEDGE STATE -> update over time. ... Probability primarily helps with the extraction from imperfect information, while Logic helps determine consequences and relationships.
a_rows_sample.statement: Gives the full revised pipeline diagram: IDEAL STATE (defines expected/relevant structure) -> OBSERVED REALITY -> INFORMATION -> EXTRACTION (branching into evidence and uncertainty) -> COMPARISON (ideal<->observed) -> LOGIC -> DETERMINATION -> FACTS -> KNOWLEDGE STATE -> update over time; probability primarily helps with extraction from imperfect information, logic helps determine consequences and relationships.

a_rows_sample.anchor: before determination, we now need to investigate: What is the Ideal State? Because determination is: D_t = Compare(Observed_t, Ideal_t) and if we don't understand Ideal_t, we don't fully understand D_t. ... IDEAL STATE -> OBSERVATION -> EXTRACTION -> COMPARISON -> DETERMINATION -> FACT -> KNOWLEDGE
a_rows_sample.statement: Revises the research direction: before determination can be understood, 'What is the Ideal State?' must be investigated, since determination is formalized as D_t=Compare(Observed_t,Ideal_t) and understanding D_t requires understanding Ideal_t; sets the research sequence as IDEAL STATE -> OBSERVATION -> EXTRACTION -> COMPARISON -> DETERMINATION -> FACT -> KNOWLEDGE, with Probability->uncertain extraction and Logic->comparison and consequence.

a_rows_sample.anchor: the fundamental question for KnowledgeOS is not "How do we store Knowledge?" and not even "How do we extract Knowledge?" It may be: "How is an ideal state of Knowledge defined, and how does a system continuously determine its current relationship to that ideal state?" ... Knowledge becomes the currently justified representation of the relationship between them. I would now research Ideal State / normative state / complete state / target state / possible-world state / domain model / epistemic idealization across mathematics, epistemology, AI, systems theory, DDD, and philosophy before we touch the Kernel again.
a_rows_sample.statement: States what may be 'the biggest discovery so far': the fundamental KnowledgeOS question may be neither 'how do we store Knowledge' nor 'how do we extract Knowledge' but 'how is an ideal state of Knowledge defined, and how does a system continuously determine its current relationship to that ideal state?'; Knowledge becomes the currently justified representation of the relationship between Ideal State and Observed State. Proposes researching Ideal State / normative state / complete state / target state / possible-world state / domain model / epistemic idealization across mathematics, epistemology, AI, systems theory, DDD, and philosophy before returning to Kernel definition.

a_rows_sample.anchor: "Every information" you mean all possible information about the thing, not merely "some information." So your proposition is: I_t = the totality of all possible information about the object/domain at time t. And I_t may be infinite.
a_rows_sample.statement: Reinterprets 'every information' as meaning ALL possible information about a thing, not merely some information: I_t is redefined as the totality of all possible information about the object/domain at time t, and I_t may be infinite -- a much stronger interpretation than given previously.

a_rows_sample.anchor: O_t subset I_t or, more realistically, imperfect projections of I_t. The extraction process is therefore: I_t -> observable information -> extracted knowledge, with the extraction being imperfect because the underlying elements can overlap and the observation process cannot completely distinguish them.
a_rows_sample.statement: A human/system cannot access all of the (possibly infinite) I_t, only observations O_t subset I_t or imperfect projections of it; extraction is I_t -> observable information -> extracted knowledge, imperfect because underlying elements can overlap and observation cannot completely distinguish them.

a_rows_sample.anchor: K = the space of all possible information/knowledge elements ... I_t subset K is the complete/ideal information state relevant at that time. Then an observer A has only an extracted state: K_t^A subset I_t ... K_t^A != I_t in general.
a_rows_sample.statement: Sharpens 'Knowledge is a state and subset of elements of the infinite Knowledge Space' into: K-script (the space of all possible information/knowledge elements), with I_t subset K-script being the complete/ideal information state relevant at time t; an observer A has only an extracted state K_t^A subset I_t (or a representation/projection of it), and because extraction is imperfect, K_t^A != I_t in general.

a_rows_sample.anchor: P(x in I_t | O_{<=t}^A). So probability describes the extraction uncertainty. ... Knowledge itself is not probability. Rather: Probability can describe the imperfect extraction of Knowledge from the ideal information state.
a_rows_sample.statement: For an ideal-state element x in I_t that an observer cannot directly verify, the observer estimates P(x in I_t | O_{<=t}^A) given its observations -- probability describes extraction uncertainty, consistent with 'the elements overlap and only probability can extract them as separately as possible' (still to be tested as the right mathematical mechanism, but a coherent hypothesis). Knowledge itself is not probability; probability describes the imperfect extraction of Knowledge from the ideal information state.

a_rows_sample.anchor: If I_t means all possible information, then we need to distinguish: possible information from true information and knowable information. ... whether your I_t means: 1. all logically possible information, or 2. all information that is actually true about the thing at t, or 3. all information that could in principle be known about the thing at t. I think this distinction is now the next critical question.
a_rows_sample.statement: Raises the next critical question: since not every possible description of a system is true, I_t must be disambiguated among three readings -- (1) all logically possible information, (2) all information that is actually true about the thing at t, or (3) all information that could in principle be known about the thing at t; this distinction will determine the meaning of the 'infinite Knowledge Space' and what KnowledgeOS is trying to extract from it.

a_rows_sample.anchor: I_t = the potentially infinite space of all relevant states/propositions/relationships at time t ... K_t (script) = Infinite Knowledge Space at t and I_t subset K_t (script) could represent an ideal state/configuration of the domain. But even I_t may itself be infinite. ... K_t = Pi_t(I_t) where Pi_t is the extraction/projection available to the observer.
a_rows_sample.statement: If I_t can be infinite, it should not be modeled as a finite list of facts but as the potentially infinite space of all relevant states/propositions/relationships at t; introduces K-script_t (infinite Knowledge Space at t) with I_t subset K-script_t as an ideal state/configuration of the domain (itself possibly infinite), and the observer's actual accessible/extracted knowledge as K_t subset I_t or, more generally, K_t=Pi_t(I_t) where Pi_t is the observer's extraction/projection function.

a_rows_sample.anchor: I_t={x_1,x_2,x_3,...}. We cannot observe all of them. ... construct an estimate hat-I_t from the observations. For an element x: P(x in I_t | O_{<=t},C_t) can express our uncertainty ... probability is increasingly looking like a mathematics of extraction from an incompletely observable/infinite state, rather than a definition of Knowledge.
a_rows_sample.statement: With an infinite ideal state I_t={x_1,x_2,...} that cannot be fully observed, an estimate hat-I_t is constructed from observations O_{<=t}, and for an element x, P(x in I_t | O_{<=t},C_t) expresses uncertainty about membership; probability is increasingly a mathematics of extraction from an incompletely observable/infinite state, not a definition of Knowledge.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Lord \overset{\text{lens}}{\longrightarrow} \Omega ... Observe the theological notion of Lord as if it were an infinite, non-exhaustible knowledge space.
b_rows_sample.statement: Rejects 'Lord = Knowledge Space' as a mathematical identity (that would turn a theological claim into a mathematical one) and replaces it with 'Lord --lens--> Ω': observing Lord AS IF an infinite knowledge space, as a thought experiment, not a metaphysical claim.

b_rows_sample.anchor: K_t \text{ is a projection; } \Omega \text{ is not exhausted by } K_t
b_rows_sample.statement: Under the Ω lens, K_t ⊆ Ω is sharpened into an explicit asymmetry: K_t is a projection of Ω, and Ω is never exhausted by K_t; the document says this is 'perhaps the strongest thing this document teaches us'.

b_rows_sample.anchor: outside current knowledge: not observed / not searched / not conceptualized / not represented / unresolved / inaccessible / not applicable / explicitly absent / genuinely nonexistent
b_rows_sample.statement: Enumerates nine distinct species of 'outside current knowledge' (not observed, not searched, not conceptualized, not represented, unresolved, inaccessible, not applicable, explicitly absent, genuinely nonexistent), presented as a richer replacement for a flat UNKNOWN category.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Whenever we create a KnowledgeOS object, ask: Are we treating our representation as though the represented thing were identical to the representation? ... Representation ≠ represented reality ... Useful representation ≠ independently existing entity
b_rows_sample.statement: Proposes using Sat/Mithya/Asat (ultimately real / appearing-but-not-independently-real / non-existent) not as statuses to implement, but as a reification test applied to every KnowledgeOS object: is the representation being treated as identical to the represented thing? Yields the anti-reification rule 'Representation ≠ represented reality' and 'Useful representation ≠ independently existing entity'.

b_rows_sample.anchor: The 'knowledge element' may therefore be a constructed epistemic representation, rather than an atomic thing discovered in reality.
b_rows_sample.statement: Applying Mithya/Zero to e ∈ K_t: a 'knowledge element' may be a constructed chain (Evidence -> Interpretation -> Claim -> Qualification -> Representation) rather than an atomic thing discovered in reality; aligns with the existing discipline 'Kernel ≠ Aggregate; Aggregate ≠ Bounded Context; Assessment ≠ State; Event ≠ Relationship; Admission ≠ Interpretation' and states the general rule 'Do not reify the abstraction merely because it is useful.'

b_rows_sample.anchor: More observations ≠ deeper understanding ... More dimensions ≠ more complete knowledge
b_rows_sample.statement: Derives from the higher/lower-knowledge distinction a research constraint: accumulating more observations or discovering more dimensions must not be equated with deeper or more complete understanding — knowing many appearances is distinct from knowing the underlying principle/substrate through which appearances are understood.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Question -> Inquiry -> Observation -> Interpretation -> Response -> Further Question -> Revision ... knowledge is not necessarily an object produced by extraction. It may be the trace of an inquiry process.
b_rows_sample.statement: Contrasts the typical KnowledgeOS pipeline (Source -> Extraction -> Knowledge) with a Q&A/inquiry-based alternative (Question -> Inquiry -> Observation -> Interpretation -> Response -> Further Question -> Revision), proposing that knowledge may be the trace of an inquiry process rather than an object produced by extraction, consistent with prior lifecycle/Quine work on revision without erasing prior existence.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Jagrat -> Swapna -> Sushupti -> Turiya ... State change ≠ Identity change ... Could the thing that persists be more fundamental than the states through which it is observed?
b_rows_sample.statement: Uses the four states of consciousness (Jagrat/Swapna/Sushupti/Turiya) and the persistence of the knower across them to restate/strengthen the already-reached position (via Quine and the Identity lens) that state change ≠ identity change, and to pose the more radical framing that a persistent relational identity may be more fundamental than any of the states through which it is observed, i.e. 'state should not own identity.'

b_rows_sample.anchor: Knowledge ≠ collection of isolated elements ... Knowledge = Elements + Relations + Context + History ... Zero applies not only to nodes ... but also to edges
b_rows_sample.statement: Extends the topological/relational lesson that knowledge is not a collection of isolated elements but Elements + Relations + Context + History, then extends Zero itself to apply to edges/relations r(e_i,e_j) (known/unknown/not-assessed/unresolved/absent/not-represented), not only to nodes e ∉ K.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Table: Lens | If Lord is observed as infinite Ω | What it teaches KnowledgeOS (ZERO, Vāṇī, Tripuṭī, Viveka, Nyāya, Topology, DDD, Identity, Lifecycle, Ontology, Śiva–Śakti, Trustee)
b_rows_sample.statement: Provides a 12-row table mapping each of twelve lenses (Zero, Vāṇī, Tripuṭī, Viveka, Nyāya, Topology, DDD, Identity, Lifecycle, Ontology, Śiva-Śakti, Trustee) applied to 'Lord as Ω' to a specific KnowledgeOS lesson, observing that most of these lessons tell KnowledgeOS 'what not to assume' rather than what to build.

b_rows_sample.anchor: What assumption does this philosophy make visible that our engineering model might otherwise hide? ... Why did you assume that the thing you are representing is the ultimate object of knowing? ... then Zero asks: What disappeared from the model when you made that assumption?
b_rows_sample.statement: Proposes a general methodological role for philosophical texts in this research: not to prove or validate the KnowledgeOS architecture, but to act as an adversarial lens exposing hidden assumptions, paired with Zero asking what disappeared from the model when an assumption was made.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Can a finite epistemic representation establish that it has exhausted the space of possible knowledge? ... No finite representation should silently infer exhaustion ... K_t ⊆ Ω is safer than K_t = Ω
b_rows_sample.statement: Reframes the research question from 'is Knowledge Space infinite?' to 'can a finite epistemic representation establish that it has exhausted the space of possible knowledge?', concluding no finite representation should silently infer exhaustion unless it has an explicit completeness argument relative to a defined universe of discourse; therefore K_t ⊆ Ω is safer than K_t = Ω, and Ω itself should be treated as a model construct, not an empirically enumerated thing.

b_rows_sample.anchor: The finite knower does not merely possess a smaller portion of an infinite knowledge space. The finite knower also determines, through its language, questions, concepts, instruments, and lenses, what portion of the space can appear as knowledge at all. ... I may not know what counts as a "thing" yet.
b_rows_sample.statement: States the document's deepest conclusion: the finite knower does not just hold a smaller portion of an infinite space, but its own language/questions/concepts/instruments/lenses determine what portion of the space CAN appear as knowledge at all — deeper than 'I know 100 of 1000 things', it is 'I may not know what counts as a thing yet', called 'Zero at its deepest level'.

b_rows_sample.anchor: I would not conclude from this: "Knowledge is consciousness." That is the theological conclusion of the source, not something our KnowledgeOS research has established. ... Never confuse the space we can represent with the totality of what can be known.
b_rows_sample.statement: Explicitly refuses to adopt the source's theological conclusion ('Knowledge is consciousness'), scoping the takeaway to three preserved boxed principles: never confuse the space we can represent with the totality of what can be known; never confuse what is currently unrepresented with what does not exist; never confuse a useful appearance/model with the reality it represents — framed as a stronger foundation for the Infinite Knowledge Space hypothesis than the word 'infinite' itself.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Knowledge is not a collection of facts; it is a self-revealing, infinite, non-exhaustible reality that illuminates all particular knowledge while remaining distinct from it.
b_rows_sample.statement: The document's own initial core-insight statement ('knowledge is a self-revealing, infinite, non-exhaustible reality'), which the document's own later review section explicitly labels a philosophical (not KnowledgeOS) conclusion and replaces with an operational definition: 'KnowledgeOS should treat knowledge as an evolving, structured representation of observations, statements, dimensions, values, relationships, evidence and reasoning within a potentially unbounded knowledge space,' plus the caveat 'the representation must not be mistaken for the totality of what can be known or for reality itself.'

b_rows_sample.anchor: smaller than the smallest imaginable object and larger than the largest imaginable object ... Ω contains both the most specific and the most general knowledge
b_rows_sample.statement: Maps the Upanishadic 'smaller than smallest, larger than largest' attribute to Ω simultaneously containing micro-level and macro-level descriptions; the self-critique accepts the structural insight (not the metaphysical mapping) and derives that a 'dimension' may itself be hierarchical/decomposable (e.g. Nexus > Infrastructure > Host > CPU), posing the open question 'are dimensions themselves decomposable into dimensions?'

b_rows_sample.anchor: Ω is both immanent and transcendent to any knowledge state ... Every knowledge element exists within a larger semantic space that contains relationships and dimensions not represented by that element. ... Element ≠ Space ... State ≠ Space
b_rows_sample.statement: Accepts and strengthens the 'inside and outside' mapping (K_t ⊂ Ω but Ω ⊄ K_t) into two general principles: Element ≠ Space, and State ≠ Space — no knowledge element or state may be treated as the complete reality it is embedded in.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Accessibility ≠ Exhaustion ... The distance between current knowledge and an unbounded/global knowledge space is not necessarily measurable, whereas bounded knowledge domains can admit meaningful completeness measures.
b_rows_sample.statement: Refines the 'near yet far' mapping: accepts Accessibility ≠ Exhaustion (you can access more without a measurable '100%'), but corrects the document's stronger claim ('distance between known/unknown is not measurable') as too strong — bounded domains (e.g. '7 of 10 mandatory controls assessed') CAN admit meaningful completeness measures even though the unbounded/global space cannot.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Knowledge extraction is revelation, not creation. ... Discovery ≠ Creation ... but Representation/Interpretation can be constructed
b_rows_sample.statement: Explicitly rejects the document's own 'revealed, not created' claim as a KnowledgeOS fact: new knowledge (e.g. 'Nexus is outdated', derived from Version=2.69, RequiredVersion=3.85, Rule) is constructed via observation/measurement/interpretation/abstraction/theory/derivation/model-construction, not merely revealed; the underlying situation existed but the derived representation was constructed. Net rule: Discovery ≠ Creation, but Representation/Interpretation can be constructed.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Jagrat->Active, Swapna->Imaginative, Sushupti->Latent, Turiya->Knowledge Space itself ... As a KnowledgeOS architecture, I would currently reject it. ... Latent ≠ Unknown ... Unrepresented: Derivable / Discoverable / Unknown dimension / Currently inaccessible
b_rows_sample.statement: Rejects the four-consciousness-states-as-KnowledgeOS-states mapping as importing theology into architecture ('too literal'), reframing it instead as the open question 'can knowledge have different epistemic modes?'; salvages 'latent knowledge' as a genuinely useful but distinct notion from 'unknown' — latent means potentially constructible/derivable from existing structure (e.g. deriving 'Outdated' from Version/Required/Rule) — and proposes a four-way taxonomy of 'Unrepresented': Derivable, Discoverable, Unknown dimension, Currently inaccessible.

a_notations: IDEAL STATE -> OBSERVATION -> EXTRACTION -> COMPARISON -> DETERMINATION -> FACT -> KNOWLEDGE
b_aliases: Lord as infinite knowledge space thought experiment

a_rows_sample.anchor: If identity is wrong, then Evidence->Claim->Model->Decision can all be mathematically correct about the wrong object. That is one of the most dangerous classes of epistemic failure
a_rows_sample.statement: Frames identity error as one of the most dangerous epistemic failure classes: correct reasoning about the wrong object.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Identity from Similarity from Equivalence from Reference. They are not interchangeable. Similarity(x,y) does not imply x=y
a_rows_sample.statement: Distinguishes identity, similarity, equivalence, and reference as non-interchangeable concepts.

a_rows_sample.anchor: R1 = nexus3.dgverlag.de, R2 = 10.61.133.85, R3 = Nexus repository server, R4 = Nexus OSS 3.69.0 host ... Denotes(R_1)=Denotes(R_2)? That requires evidence. A name is not the entity
a_rows_sample.statement: Worked four-reference Nexus example illustrating reference-vs-entity denotation requiring evidence.

a_rows_sample.anchor: denotes:R->E. r_1=r_2 is not required for denotes(r_1)=denotes(r_2). Different references can identify the same entity
a_rows_sample.statement: Formally defines the denotes function from references to entities.

a_rows_sample.anchor: server01 in Environment=A and server01 in Environment=B. Name(x)=Name(y) does not imply x=y
a_rows_sample.statement: Worked counterexample of identical names denoting different entities across environments.

a_rows_sample.anchor: denotes(r,c) -> e where c is context. This is strongly aligned with DDD. The same linguistic term can have different meanings in different bounded contexts
a_rows_sample.statement: Extends denotation to be context-relative, aligned with DDD.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Customer exists in Sales and Billing ... may correspond to the same real-world person or organization, but they are not automatically the same domain object. RealWorldIdentity != DomainObjectIdentity
a_rows_sample.statement: Worked Customer/Sales/Billing example establishing RealWorldIdentity != DomainObjectIdentity.

a_rows_sample.anchor: KnowledgeOS must not globally impose GlobalEntityIdentity where the domain has intentionally defined separate identities. Instead Identity is contextual
a_rows_sample.statement: States one of the most important DDD principles for KnowledgeOS: identity is contextual, not globally imposed.

a_rows_sample.anchor: entity resolution asks P(SameEntity|r_1,r_2,C). But this immediately introduces uncertainty
a_rows_sample.statement: Defines entity resolution as a probabilistic inference problem.

a_rows_sample.anchor: P(SameEntity)=0.97. That does not mean SameEntity=True. It means the evidence supports a high probability under a specified model. This must remain distinct from confirmed identity
a_rows_sample.statement: Distinguishes probabilistic entity-resolution confidence from confirmed identity.

a_rows_sample.anchor: IdentityStatus in {Unknown, Candidate, Probable, Confirmed, Rejected, Contextual}. This is much safer than forcing binary identity too early
a_rows_sample.statement: Defines a six-value graded identity-status taxonomy.

a_rows_sample.anchor: r_1 and r_2 have matching hostname; IP; service port; environment. We may create CandidateSameEntity(r_1,r_2). But not yet ConfirmedSameEntity
a_rows_sample.statement: Defines candidate identity as distinct from confirmed identity, worked with a multi-attribute-match example.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Confirmation might require DNS, CMDB, RuntimeObservation, or HumanConfirmation. The confirmation mechanism becomes provenance
a_rows_sample.statement: Defines identity-confirmation evidence sources and their provenance role.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Identity itself becomes an epistemic claim: A: denotes(r_1)=denotes(r_2). Then all Step 32-37 machinery applies: Evidence->Assertion->Validation->Confidence->Decision
a_rows_sample.statement: States identity is itself an epistemic claim subject to the full evidence/validation/confidence/decision machinery.

a_rows_sample.anchor: We should therefore reject the idea that identity resolution is merely a database lookup ... when identity is ambiguous IdentityResolution is an epistemic inference problem
a_rows_sample.statement: Argues identity resolution is often an epistemic inference problem, not merely a database lookup.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Reflexivity x=x. Symmetry x=y=>y=x. Transitivity x=y and y=z=>x=z. These properties matter
a_rows_sample.statement: Restates the formal reflexivity/symmetry/transitivity properties of equality.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Similarity(A,B) and Similarity(B,C). It does not follow that Similarity(A,C). Therefore similarity cannot automatically be treated as equality
a_rows_sample.statement: States similarity is not necessarily transitive, unlike equality.

a_rows_sample.anchor: sim(A,B)=0.95, sim(B,C)=0.95 but sim(A,C)=0.60. If we merge A and B, and B and C, we may accidentally merge A and C
a_rows_sample.statement: Worked counterexample of transitive-closure contamination from thresholded similarity merging.

a_rows_sample.anchor: A false merge means x!=y but KnowledgeOS stores x=y. Consequences: incorrect evidence aggregation; false conflicts; incorrect history; contaminated statistics; wrong ownership; wrong decisions. This is a high-severity epistemic failure
a_rows_sample.statement: Defines false merge and its six categories of consequence as a high-severity failure mode.

a_rows_sample.anchor: The reverse is x=y but KnowledgeOS stores x!=y. Consequences: duplicated knowledge; missed contradictions; fragmented provenance; incorrect counts; duplicated investigations. Both errors matter
a_rows_sample.statement: Defines false split and its five categories of consequence.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Inference asks what can we conclude from what we know. Step 34 asks What should we learn next? ... a fundamentally different problem
b_rows_sample.statement: Distinguishes inference from information-acquisition selection as fundamentally different problems.

b_rows_sample.anchor: 10^6 uncertain assertions ... impossible and unnecessary to validate all of them immediately ... Choose the information acquisition action that produces the greatest useful improvement relative to its cost
b_rows_sample.statement: States KnowledgeOS should not investigate everything, requiring a cost-relative optimization.

b_rows_sample.anchor: QueryCMDB, InspectRuntime, AskDomainExpert, RunTest, PerformExperiment, RetrieveDocument, CompareIndependentSource ... produces an observation Y_I
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines the information-gathering action set with seven worked examples.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Cost(I) ... Time, Money, Compute, HumanAttention, OperationalRisk ... information is not free
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines Cost(I) across five components.

b_rows_sample.anchor: EVPI=L_0-L_{PI} ... an upper bound on the value of information
b_rows_sample.statement: Formally defines Expected Value of Perfect Information as an upper bound.

b_rows_sample.anchor: EVSI(I)=L_0-E_Y[\min_d E[L(d,\theta)\mid K,Y]] ... NVOI(I)=EVSI(I)-Cost(I) ... the core mathematical idea
b_rows_sample.statement: Formally defines Expected Value of Sample Information and net value of information as the step's core idea.

b_rows_sample.anchor: I^*=\arg\max_{I\in\mathcal I}NVOI(I) ... our first formal definition of NextBestEpistemicAction
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines the first formal Next-Best-Epistemic-Action.

b_rows_sample.anchor: InformationValue\neq UncertaintyReduction ... A has no influence on any important decision ... UncertaintyReduction(A) may have almost zero practical value
b_rows_sample.statement: States the subtle principle that information value is not the same as uncertainty reduction.

b_rows_sample.anchor: DecisionSensitivity(A,D) ... Information about A is valuable if learning A can change d^*
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines DecisionSensitivity as the criterion for information value.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Nexus has 31 GB RAM ... migration architecture does not depend on RAM beyond a very large safety margin ... almost no decision value
b_rows_sample.statement: Worked example of low-decision-sensitivity uncertainty (RAM precision beyond safety margin).

b_rows_sample.anchor: Production database backup is restorable ... DecisionSensitivity(B,D) is very high ... validating B may have extremely high VOI
b_rows_sample.statement: Worked contrasting example of high-decision-sensitivity uncertainty (backup restorability).

b_rows_sample.anchor: d^*=f(K) ... If perturbing A does not change f(K), then A has low local decision sensitivity
b_rows_sample.statement: Formalizes a decision-relevance partition via perturbation of the decision function.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Closure(A) ... A\rightarrow B\rightarrow D ... DependencyClosure+DecisionCriticality=EpistemicPrioritization
b_rows_sample.statement: Combines Step 32's dependency closure with decision dependency, giving a prioritization formula.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Criticality(D) ... Low, Medium, High, Critical ... should be domain-owned. KnowledgeOS can consume it but should not invent the business meaning
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines a domain-owned Criticality classification, not invented by KnowledgeOS.

b_rows_sample.anchor: EL(d)=E[L(d,\theta)\mid K] ... d^*=\arg\min_d EL(d) ... d_1 expected loss 10, d_2 expected loss 12 ... investigation may reveal a high-risk state in which d_2 becomes preferable
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines expected loss and current-optimal decision, worked with a two-decision expected-loss-reversal example.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Risk<5\%\Rightarrow AutomaticApproval ... Risk\in[3\%,8\%] ... DecisionBoundaryUncertainty. Uncertainty far from a decision boundary may be harmless. Uncertainty near a boundary can be critical
b_rows_sample.statement: Introduces DecisionBoundaryUncertainty, worked with a threshold-straddling risk-interval example.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Risk\in[1\%,2\%] ... no urgent investigation ... Risk\in[4\%,7\%] crosses the decision boundary ... additional evidence is valuable
b_rows_sample.statement: Worked contrasting examples of harmless-far and critical-boundary-straddling risk intervals.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Priority(A)\propto DecisionImpact(A)\times Uncertainty(A) ... conceptual, not yet a universal formula
b_rows_sample.statement: Proposes a conceptual, not-yet-universal epistemic-triage priority formula.

b_rows_sample.anchor: EVSI(I)=10, Cost(I)=2, NVOI(I)=8 ... EVSI=12, Cost=20, NVOI=-8 ... should not be prioritized merely because it provides more information
b_rows_sample.statement: Worked arithmetic example showing higher-EVSI investigations can have lower net value once cost is subtracted.

b_rows_sample.anchor: HumanAttention is an epistemic resource ... 2 hours of a senior architect's time may be more expensive than a machine-readable check
b_rows_sample.statement: States human attention is itself a costed epistemic resource, worked with a comparison example.

a_rows_sample.anchor: one aggregate with two parts, or two aggregates sharing an identity? ... I-4 is itself a spanning invariant — a negative one.
a_rows_sample.statement: Facing evidence that no positive invariant spans the lifecycle and authority parts of the record (an honest finding that argues for splitting), the proposal nonetheless keeps one root because I-4 (they must never merge) is a negative spanning invariant needing a single holder that can see both parts, and the write boundary is one file.

a_rows_sample.anchor: (D) invariant violation — NO ... (D), and the defect is in the proposal's I-5 row, not in the invariant, the mechanism, or the model.
a_rows_sample.statement: C-3's classification is independently derived (before reading the refinement's own reasoning) as (D): the observed non-Governance recorder on a HANDOFF transition is not an invariant violation, missing enforcement, or a missing conceptual distinction, but simply a table cell in the proposal that measured I-5 (an authority-part invariant) against a lifecycle-part transition, which I-4 itself forbids conflating.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Verdict: (D) — a mis-scoped invariant statement. ... D.1 — The observation and the invariant live in different parts of the aggregate.
a_rows_sample.statement: Independent classification (derived from evidence E-1..E-8 before considering any candidate) concludes (D): the observed `architecture`-recorded HANDOFF is not a violation, missing enforcement, or missing distinction, but a case of measuring an authority-part invariant (I-5) against a lifecycle-part transition, which I-4 itself forbids; both instances were also the mechanism's required actor (DP-3), and a HANDOFF confers no ownership regardless.

a_rows_sample.anchor: OQ-12 | Should invariants carry an explicit enforcement class — refused · overwritten · not-consulted · writer obligation? ... OQ-13 | Is authorizationLinkage a modelling element or a query convenience?
a_rows_sample.statement: Two new open questions are raised without proposed solutions: whether invariants should carry an explicit enforcement class distinguishing refused/overwritten/not-consulted/writer-obligation (OQ-12), and whether the identity query's authorizationLinkage is a modelling element or mere query convenience (OQ-13).

a_rows_sample.anchor: 'Consistency is determined by invariant ownership, not by event-driven communication.' ... EKS: No event bus. Yet: 11/11 workflow invariants → single identifiable owner → executable tests ... SUPPORTED: non-distributed systems / UNKNOWN: distributed KnowledgeOS
a_rows_sample.statement: DeepSeek tests and finds current consistency is achieved through invariant ownership, not event-driven integration: EKS has no event bus yet 11/11 workflow invariants have a single identifiable owner with executable tests; PKS has no event architecture yet governance invariants define ownership; AIP has no event-driven architecture yet BC-7 mechanically owns orchestration invariants. Explicitly does NOT over-generalize: classified SUPPORTED for non-distributed systems, UNKNOWN for a distributed KnowledgeOS.

a_rows_sample.anchor: C-17 Authority enforcement ... E — MISSING ... C-18 Temporal reconstruction of authority ... 2/218 transitions carry any date field ... E — MISSING ... C-19 Cross-process coordination / provenance attestation ... E — MISSING ... C-20 Delegation ... OBSERVED BEHAVIOUR — SEMANTIC INTERPRETATION UNKNOWN
a_rows_sample.statement: Of 22 catalogued EKS capabilities (C-01..C-22, mostly class A implemented), four stand out as gaps: C-17 Authority enforcement is class E (MISSING, no implementation evidence at all); C-18 Temporal reconstruction of authority is class E (only 2/218 transitions carry any date field); C-19 Cross-process coordination/provenance attestation is class E; C-20 Delegation is explicitly re-classified (an archaeology-hardening correction) as 'OBSERVED BEHAVIOUR — SEMANTIC INTERPRETATION UNKNOWN' rather than implemented-but-implicit, since 0/126 grants carry any delegation, validity, expiry, ownership, or session-linkage field.

a_rows_sample.anchor: 11 of 11 workflow-record invariants have a single, identifiable owner and an executable test. Every invariant outside the workflow record either has no owner or has an advisory-only owner.
a_rows_sample.statement: Invariant-ownership table finding: all 11 workflow-record invariants (Inv A-J, G-2/G-3, R8) have a single identifiable code owner and an executable test (mostly class A); by contrast grant-identity uniqueness, temporal ordering of authority, and process/actor authenticity have NO owner at all (class E), while corpus reference integrity, identifier uniqueness, document schema conformance, and placement correctness have only advisory-only owners (class C) -- 'every invariant outside the workflow record either has no owner or has an advisory-only owner.'

a_rows_sample.anchor: I-4 registry != authority, never merged; I-10 the record outranks prose
a_rows_sample.statement: AIP's own invariant: I-4 registry != authority, never merged; I-10 the record outranks prose. The authority record is the per-work-item transition+grant log; the session registry is separate and is not authority.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Mechanically enforced invariants ... all contract-pinned by tests
a_rows_sample.statement: Mechanically enforced (contract-pinned by tests): I-1 exactly one mutation owner; I-2 HANDOFF and human START (neither alone yields ACTIVE); I-3 STOPPED is sticky (only CONTINUATION exits); G-1 closure is a governance act (COMPLETE refuses non-governance writers); G-2 Authority State has exactly one writer (grant writer rule R5a/R5b).

a_rows_sample.anchor: Declared-only invariants (NOT mechanically enforced)
a_rows_sample.statement: Declared but not mechanically enforced: R-34 producer != acceptor; INV-ATTR-2 separation is declared, not attestable; AIP-11 supersede-never-in-place; AIP-14 Product Primacy; I-4 registry != authority, never merged; I-10 the record outranks prose.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Every invariant BC-7 (the workflow engine) owns is mechanically enforced; almost every invariant outside BC-7 is declared only
a_rows_sample.statement: Headline structural finding -- the invariant asymmetry: assurance is strong where it is executable (BC-7) and weak where it is prose (outside BC-7). 'The platform mechanically protects orchestration, and protects knowledge/verification/communication only by declaration.' Stated as the single most important structural property of AIP's current architecture.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Headline structural findings
a_rows_sample.statement: Seven headline findings: (1) AIP is a registry-first, session-based engineering operating platform, not a product domain; (2) the implemented core is the workflow/authority engine plus guard surfaces, with knowledge/review components deferred/not built and verification under construction; (3) the invariant asymmetry is the load-bearing structural property; (4) the authority record lives in an ignored runtime directory (the durability inversion), decided-but-not-executed; (5) the D1/D2 decision state is contradictory across the corpus, surfaced not reconciled; (6) four unowned capabilities form one control loop with C-10/C-14 existence UNDECIDED; (7) AIP self-records four capability failures (EKS-01..04) -- the platform observing its own uneven assurance.

a_rows_sample.anchor: IMPLEMENTED != VERIFIED != ADOPTED != AUTHORIZED (§38) -- this review establishes readiness for the fourth-to-third transition and leaves ADOPTED and AUTHORIZED untouched.
a_rows_sample.statement: Confirms and applies the four-state lifecycle model (IMPLEMENTED, VERIFIED, ADOPTED, AUTHORIZED as four distinct, non-collapsible states, §38) as load-bearing governance vocabulary: a PASS review moves work from VERIFIED toward being ready for the ADOPTED decision, but does not itself adopt or authorize, and the adoption decision belongs solely to the PO/ARB.

a_rows_sample.anchor: IMPLEMENTED the capability, document and contract test were produced (this slice) / VERIFIED independent verification of the produced work (PENDING) / ADOPTED governance-path adoption decision by the PO/ARB (PENDING) / AUTHORIZED authorized for future use as the operating model (PENDING)
a_rows_sample.statement: Originates the four-state completion model (IMPLEMENTED / VERIFIED / ADOPTED / AUTHORIZED) as a required, never-collapsed distinction in the implementing session's completion report -- the same model later confirmed and applied throughout S0374-S0382.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Candidate A — Work Item Aggregate ... Result: passes every test. Critically, all four invariants are internal to it
b_rows_sample.statement: WorkItem is tested and confirmed as the aggregate root: its identity, lifecycle, four invariants (I-1..I-4), and consistency boundary are all internal to a single JSON record, needing no cross-record data to enforce.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Candidate B — Assignment Aggregate (rejected) ... I-1 is an invariant over the set of assignments, not over one.
b_rows_sample.statement: Assignment is rejected as aggregate root because the single-mutation-owner invariant (I-1) spans the whole set of assignments and cannot be stated from inside one, and HANDOFF is atomic across two assignments, making Assignment an entity inside WorkItem, not a root.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Candidate C — Workflow Aggregate (rejected — and reclassified) ... Workflow is a Value Object on the root, not an aggregate.
b_rows_sample.statement: Workflow is rejected as aggregate root (it is a fixed classifier with no lifecycle or state of its own) and reclassified as a Value Object on the WorkItem root.

b_rows_sample.anchor: one aggregate with two parts, or two aggregates sharing an identity? ... I-4 is itself a spanning invariant — a negative one.
b_rows_sample.statement: Facing evidence that no positive invariant spans the lifecycle and authority parts of the record (an honest finding that argues for splitting), the proposal nonetheless keeps one root because I-4 (they must never merge) is a negative spanning invariant needing a single holder that can see both parts, and the write boundary is one file.

b_rows_sample.anchor: WorkItem [aggregate root] ... LIFECYCLE PART ... AUTHORITY PART ... DERIVED BY FOLD — never stored, never settable
b_rows_sample.statement: The proposed tactical model formalizes WorkItem as the aggregate root with a never-merged lifecycle part (transitions, assignments) and authority part (grants), plus derived-by-fold-only fields (workItemState, assignmentState, mutationOwner) that must never be stored or settable.

b_rows_sample.anchor: OQ-9 One aggregate or two (RA-4)? ... the single largest structural choice in the model
b_rows_sample.statement: Eleven open questions (OQ-1..OQ-11) are carried, explicitly not decided: role-model ownership deferred to ADR-AIP-04, session-name uniqueness scope, whether CONTINUATION/FAIL are real or dead vocabulary (0/117 observed), whether Grant is an entity or immutable record, and whether one or two aggregates is correct (flagged as the single largest structural choice).

b_rows_sample.anchor: The proposal's claim that authorized 'never consults the session' is FALSE. The command requires --session and refuses on an unregistered session
b_rows_sample.statement: F-1: the proposal's claim that the `authorized` command never consults the session is false as written, because it requires and validates session registration as a precondition before answering, even though the verdict itself (grant-scope equality) does not use the session.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Is the WorkItem aggregate justification sufficiently supported? — YES.
b_rows_sample.statement: The verifier concludes the WorkItem aggregate justification is sufficiently supported: rejections of Assignment, Workflow, and Human Act as root are each independently re-derived and confirmed, and the F-1 correction, if anything, strengthens the one-root recommendation.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Answerability precondition ... Verdict function ... Consistency invariant ... this is the thing §4.5 was actually testing for
b_rows_sample.statement: A three-way distinction is independently confirmed and formalized to repair the F-1 wording: an answerability precondition (who may ask) is not the same kind of statement as a verdict function (what is computed) or a consistency invariant (whether two parts must agree), and only the third was what §4.5's test was actually checking for.

b_rows_sample.anchor: (D) invariant violation — NO ... (D), and the defect is in the proposal's I-5 row, not in the invariant, the mechanism, or the model.
b_rows_sample.statement: C-3's classification is independently derived (before reading the refinement's own reasoning) as (D): the observed non-Governance recorder on a HANDOFF transition is not an invariant violation, missing enforcement, or a missing conceptual distinction, but simply a table cell in the proposal that measured I-5 (an authority-part invariant) against a lifecycle-part transition, which I-4 itself forbids conflating.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Four independent verification passes, three architecture passes, one eligibility rejection, one correction cycle — the model was never accepted on its author's word.
b_rows_sample.statement: The BC-7 tactical domain model is formally accepted as refined and corrected, the registration explicitly summarizing the full assurance chain (four verification passes, three architecture passes, one eligibility rejection, one correction cycle) as evidence it was never accepted merely on its author's word.

b_rows_sample.anchor: The falsified claim appears three times ... Neither input document enumerates the sites.
b_rows_sample.statement: The refinement finds F-1's falsified 'never consults the session' claim actually appears at three separate sites in the proposal, a fuller enumeration than either the proposal or Verification #1 provided, and supplies precise replacement wording for each.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Answerability precondition ... Verdict function ... Consistency invariant ... a rule requiring a lifecycle fact and an authority fact to agree
b_rows_sample.statement: The refinement formalizes the three-way distinction (answerability precondition vs verdict function vs consistency invariant) that separates what F-1 defeats (a sentence) from what it does not defeat (the underlying one-aggregate argument), concluding the read-dependency actually strengthens rather than weakens the case for one aggregate.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Verdict: (D) — a mis-scoped invariant statement. ... D.1 — The observation and the invariant live in different parts of the aggregate.
b_rows_sample.statement: Independent classification (derived from evidence E-1..E-8 before considering any candidate) concludes (D): the observed `architecture`-recorded HANDOFF is not a violation, missing enforcement, or missing distinction, but a case of measuring an authority-part invariant (I-5) against a lifecycle-part transition, which I-4 itself forbids; both instances were also the mechanism's required actor (DP-3), and a HANDOFF confers no ownership regardless.

b_rows_sample.anchor: identity reads both parts of the aggregate in one call — and neither input document raises it. ... a work-item-scoped value presented inside a session-scoped answer

a_rows_sample.anchor: The ladder
a_rows_sample.statement: A three-status admission ladder governed by an explicit policy: Candidate -> Supported -> Accepted. Transitions form a covering relation -- each status reachable only from its immediate predecessor (I-12); skipping is formally excluded. The Supported -> Accepted transition is named Determination, governed by the AcceptancePolicy, which decides what may be admitted -- a different question from what the evidence supports.

a_rows_sample.anchor: The boundary
a_rows_sample.statement: Committed is not a fourth epistemic status; it is a decision-boundary status attached to an Accepted item by authority, under the model's sharpest rule A6: authority determines commitment, not evidential truth. Evidence can make a claim Accepted; only an authorized act can make anyone bound to it. The falsification pass caught the earlier formulation quietly treating Committed as a rung of the same ladder; the ratified repair re-typed it, and the lived governance record enacts exactly this discipline (adoption and authorization as separate human acts).

a_rows_sample.anchor: The policy governs itself — governedly
a_rows_sample.statement: The AcceptancePolicy is itself a governed, versioned object: policy-as-content (admissible like any claim, at rest inside K_t) is distinguished from policy-in-force (the approved version that actually governs admission), and no in-force policy changes without a governed decision (I-11); mentioned here because admission is where its absence would corrupt first.

a_rows_sample.anchor: The adjacent states — an inheritance
a_rows_sample.statement: The ladder answers how far admitted, never in what condition held. The ratified Final Architecture layers the constitutional state vocabulary beside it: REJECTED (failed reasoning preserved, never silently discarded), CONFLICTED (contradictory knowledge coexisting until governed resolution, the conflict record surviving resolution), and the evidence-layer triple UNKNOWN != ABSENT != FALSE. These are not extensions bolted on: the archaeology dated them to the programme's first weeks, before the ladder existed -- inherited from the constitutional side rather than invented to fill the gap.

III.10 consolidated the invariant discipline into five distinctions that must remain visible in later chapters: exists != proven; stated != tested; no contradiction != consistency proof; coherence != completeness; mathematical soundness != computability.
